oewn-01976145-v.learner: to move into a particular state or condition.
examples: seemed in danger of sinking into total silence
His affection for her soon sunk into indifference

oewn-00433792-v.learner: to fall hard or all at once, or to go down by a large amount.
examples: Her power was sinking
After the bad harvest, grain prices sank.

oewn-01990883-v.learner: to make something sink below the surface.
examples: The storm sank two fishing boats off the coast.

oewn-00585404-n.learner: the work you do to earn money.
examples: He found employment at the mill soon after he came to town.

oewn-13991539-n.learner: the state of being employed, or of having a job.
examples: She has been in employment ever since she left school.
The employment of such harsh words surprised everyone at the table.

oewn-08099479-n.learner: one of the groups of Christians that has its own beliefs and its own ways of worship.
examples: She was raised in the Methodist church and her husband in the Catholic one.

oewn-03031762-n.learner: a place where people gather for worship, especially Christian worship.
examples: the bride and bridegroom set off for Kent from the church door

oewn-01034400-n.learner: a religious service held in a building used for worship.
examples: you will have the honour of seeing Lady Catherine de Bourgh on the ensuing Sunday at church
Church begins at ten on Sunday morning.

oewn-04901232-n.learner: not being careful enough in practical matters.
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia
I see the imprudence of it.

connotation.why: attributes a failing to the person spoken of

oewn-01784021-v.learner: to be afraid or scared of something.
examples: She dreaded seeing Wickham again, and was resolved to avoid it as long as possible.
Not that I am afraid of myself, but I dread other people's remarks.

oewn-07524811-n.learner: the feeling you have when something is extremely surprising.
examples: to her utter amazement, she saw Mr. Darcy walk into the room
Mrs. Bennet found, with amazement and horror, that her husband would not advance a guinea

oewn-14430687-n.learner: a lack of patience; being annoyed by anything that makes you wait.
examples: I shall not sport with your impatience by reading what he says on that point.
Her impatience for this second letter was as well rewarded as impatience generally is.

connotation.why: names a feeling as the absence of a virtue

oewn-04649953-n.learner: a dislike of anything that makes you wait.
examples: His impatience showed in every queue he ever stood in.

connotation.why: marks a settled trait as the absence of a virtue

oewn-07529310-n.learner: a restless wish for change and excitement.
examples: A youthful impatience drove him to leave the quiet town.

oewn-07522337-n.learner: the shame you feel when other people find out that you fell short or did wrong.
examples: shaking off his embarrassment, he turned to her again
It was not to be supposed that time would give Lydia that embarrassment from which she had been so wholly free

oewn-07320169-n.learner: an event that makes someone feel embarrassed.
examples: The lost match was an embarrassment for the whole team.

oewn-14009674-n.learner: the state of being embarrassed, usually because you do not have enough money.
examples: Years of debt had left the family in real embarrassment.

oewn-04659534-n.learner: the quality of keeping things secret.
examples: Having said thus much, I feel no doubt of your secrecy.
There were few people on whose secrecy she would have more confidently depended

connotation.why: names a person's habit of concealing

oewn-14439493-n.learner: the state of being hidden or kept out of sight.
examples: unless it is, for very cogent reasons, to remain in the secrecy which Lydia seems to think necessary

oewn-00625102-n.learner: an effort that causes you trouble.
examples: I had no difficulty in believing it
I had difficulty in finding out even so much as this.

oewn-04716529-n.learner: the quality of being nearly too much for someone to handle and needing great effort to come out well.
examples: No one had warned us about the difficulty of the final climb.
